title: Cab Calloway as a first-class bandleader and the film shorts
summary: Cheatham praises Cab for paying well and on time, and recalls the Betty Boop shorts and other films made while at the Cotton Club.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Were you paid well for something like this?
We were paid very well for that, yes.

That's one thing I can say for Cab Calloway, he paid well, and paid on time. I don't think Cab was five minutes late paying off the band the whole time I was with him. He was just about the greatest business band leader that I ever worked for.
I can really say that for him. He was really first class. He saw that the band had everything they wanted, the best accommodations.
So you were recording quite a bit
Oh, yes, we made a lot of those Bettie Boop things, and all kind of shorts--
That's right you did more movie work.
Oh, yes. Did a lot of things on the train, you know, the old man of the mountain.
Were you doing these things all on that same trip out there?
No that was -- most of those were done here, while we were at the Cotton Club.
Oh, I see, I see. But when you were out in Hollywood, was it 1932, or '34?
